title: The agent that built a second badge
scenario:
A city library builds a booking app in React. The team documents its components in Storybook and wants every agent to reuse them. They installed the Storybook MCP addon. Two developers use Claude Code. After one week, the agents still build new components and copy old ones. You read the setup notes and the log.

Use the exhibit. The library, the files and the log are made up for this case. Tool details are from the vendors' pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
SETUP NOTES (made up)

  Storybook 10, framework @storybook/react-vite
  Addon: @storybook/addon-mcp (installed)
  .storybook/main.ts:
    features: {}            <- nothing set
  Claude Code: Ana added the Storybook MCP server with
    the default (local) scope. Nothing else was changed.
  Story "Button / OldStyle2024": kept to show the docs team
    the button we no longer use.
  Badge docs: one prop, variant ("info" | "warning").

WEEK 1 LOG
  1. The agent has no docs-list tool. The MCP page says
     the docs toolset is unavailable.
  2. Ben's Claude Code sessions show no Storybook tools.
     Ana's do.
  3. (after fixing 1) The agent copies the old 2024 button
     from the OldStyle2024 story into a new page.
  4. The agent writes <Badge tone="warning">. Badge has no
     tone prop.

questions.prompt: Log 1: why is the docs toolset unavailable here?

options.text: The components manifest is off by default; set componentsManifest: true
options.explanation: Right. Storybook says the components manifest is off by default. The docs toolset reads it, and react-vite can make one.

options.text: React frameworks make no manifest; move the project to another framework
options.explanation: The Storybook docs say the React frameworks generate manifests, and react-vite is a React framework.

options.text: The docs toolset needs Storybook Test, so install Storybook Test first
options.explanation: Storybook says the docs toolset reads the components manifest. Tests play no part in it, and here the manifest is off.

options.text: The MCP server runs only in a built Storybook, never on the dev server
options.explanation: The Storybook docs say you reach the MCP server while its dev server runs. The docs toolset is off because the components manifest is off by default.

questions.prompt: Log 2: Ben's sessions have no Storybook tools. What is the best fix?

options.text: Add the server again with user scope so the whole team can use it
options.explanation: User scope is private to one user account. It does not reach Ben.

options.text: Write "use the Storybook MCP" in AGENTS.md so Ben's agent connects
options.explanation: A rules file tells an agent what to do. It does not connect a server that is not set up.

options.text: Add it with project scope and check .mcp.json into version control
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says to check .mcp.json into version control so everyone on the team gets the same MCP tools.

options.text: Put the server in ~/.codex/config.toml so every agent can find it
options.explanation: That is Codex's file in one person's home folder. Ben uses Claude Code, and it is not shared.

questions.prompt: Log 3: the agent copies the old 2024 button. How do you keep that story but hide it?

options.text: Rename the story to DO NOT COPY so the agent will skip it
options.explanation: No page here says a story name keeps it out. The story would still be in the manifest.

options.text: Add tags: ['!manifest'] to that story so manifests skip it
options.explanation: Right. Removing the manifest tag keeps a story out of the manifests, for example one for instruction only.

options.text: Turn componentsManifest off again so no story reaches it
options.explanation: That hides every component, and the docs toolset stops working. Only one story needs to go.

options.text: Delete the Button docs page so the agent stops seeing it
options.explanation: That removes the docs for the button you do want reused. Hide the one story instead.

questions.prompt: Log 4: the agent wrote a tone prop that Badge does not have. Which rule follows Storybook's advice?

options.text: Allow props that are common in other libraries, such as tone
options.explanation: Storybook's example rules say not to assume props from patterns in other libraries.

options.text: Let the agent add a tone prop to Badge when a design needs one
options.explanation: That changes a shared component without asking. Storybook's rules say to check back with the user.

options.text: Install a new badge from a registry that has a tone prop on it
options.explanation: That makes a second badge, the problem this chapter is about. Use the documented variant prop.

options.text: Use only documented props, check docs-show, and ask if unsure
options.explanation: Right. Storybook's example rules: use only documented props, query docs-show, and check back with the user.
